newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN LEV REGAINS TO 229-230 PER DLR AT CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN LEV REGAINS TO 229-230 PER DLR AT CLOSE.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev traded at 229-230 per dollar at the close of the interbank matket, stronger than 235-236 in the morning due to dollar sales by the central bank, dealers said.
"For the first time in several weeks the lev closes firmer, which today was due to the active support from the central bank," a dealer said.
The lev was even stronger than yesterday's close at 234-235 to the dollar, the dealer added.

Interbank trade started in low volumes at around 235 levs per dollar, but a rise in foreign currency demand from clients on the illiquid market instantly pressured the lev to 237.50-238 per dollar around midday, dealers said.
The central bank then stepped in, offering relatively large dollar volumes initially at 232 levs per dollar and at 229-230 later, dealers said.
According to some traders the central bank sold dollars to several banks in volumes between $200,000 and $300,000 per bank to cover the demand.
Central bank officials declined comment. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
